chapter: Caravan, Perdido and the first tunes
title: How he got a royalty share in Caravan
summary: Irving Mills gave him a percentage on Caravan in return for his other tunes, with two cheques a year; his name was always going to be on it.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: How many years after you wrote Caravan did you finally get some royalties? You say Irving Mills finally put your name back on it.
Oh yeah, later on, they gave me a percentage.

Oh, I don't know; I forgot now what it was. But I know he wanted a contract to all my tunes, to get them over to Mills and this and the other, so he said, 'Well, if you leave all those tunes in here, I will give you a percentage now on Caravan.' So they gave me a percentage -- I forgot the percentage, what it was. But they were pretty nice, anyhow. They send me two checks a year. There used to be four checks, but then they cut it down to two. That's what I said about Tempo -- there should be two checks a year now; so far I've got but only one. I don't know what happened to the other one.
Back when we were talking about Caravan, you say you sold it outright to Irving Mills for $25. Was your name on it at all then?
Oh, my name was going to be on the thing anyhow.
But you just didn't get anything for it.
But not for the money business.
